title: Rapid Hypothesis Kickoff Protocol — Project Harbor
body:
Context
Project Harbor is a mid-market retail customer exploring: (a) product-recommendation reranking with contextual embeddings, and (b) a lightweight assistant for merchant support queries. This doc defines a compact, hypothesis-driven kickoff and acceptance protocol to run a 3-week proof-of-concept with clear pass/fail criteria.

Goals (top-line)
- Validate that Redwood Dedicated endpoints can support 95th percentile latency targets (<120ms per token for interactive sessions) for the merchant assistant workload at planned concurrent users.
- Demonstrate a 15-20% improvement in click-through-rate (CTR) on targeted recommendation slots using embeddings + reranking over current baseline rule-based model.
- Establish monitoring, rollback, and cost envelope guardrails so the customer can evaluate production readiness.

Hypotheses (explicit)
H1: Using a 3B open model with 8-bit quantization + prefix caching will keep median latency under 80ms and 95th under 120ms for typical 256-token sessions.
H2: Embedding similarity + light reranker (smaller transformer) will lift CTR by >= 15% when seeded with recent 7-day behavioral logs.
H3: Observability hooks (token-level tracing + per-route cost) will surface any regressions within one hour of deployment and enable rollback under SLA.

Scope (what we will and wont do)
In scope:
- 3-week POC on Redwood Dedicated reserved pool (customer-provided credentials).
- Two verticals: recommendation reranking (batch + on-demand) and merchant assistant (chat flows).
- Minimal data integration: S3 ingestion of last 30 days of anonymized event logs and product catalog snapshot.
- Basic UI demo pages for manual evaluation.

Out of scope:
- Full on-prem private deployment (will iterate after POC).
- Large-scale A/B testing across live traffic (we will use shadow traffic or sampling).

Kickoff Workshop Agenda (90 minutes)
1) 5m - Introductions and goals (owner: Maya)
2) 10m - Customer business metrics & current baseline (merchant ops lead)
3) 15m - Proposed experiment design (Jordan + Eng) 
4) 20m - Data ingestion plan and data checks (Sofia)
5) 15m - SLOs, cost envelope, and rollback strategy (SRE/Platform)
6) 15m - Success criteria and evaluation cadence (Ethan)
7) 10m - Risks, open questions, and next steps

Roles & RACI (condensed)
- Customer product lead: success signoff on business metrics (R)
- Solutions Eng (Maya, Jordan): POC design, model selection, demo (A)
- Data Eng (Sofia): ingestion + sample validation (R)
- Platform/SRE: dedicated pool provisioning, SLO monitoring (C)
- Customer SRE: network & firewall tests (I)

Success Metrics (quantitative)
- Latency: median token latency < 80ms; 95th < 120ms for conversational endpoint under defined concurrency.
- Recommendation uplift: CTR delta >= +15% over baseline in controlled sampling.
- Cost: incremental inference cost not to exceed $0.015 per generated response (customer-stated max).
- Reliability: no more than 2% error rate (5xx or model crashes) during the test window.

Acceptance Matrix (week-by-week gate)
Week 0 (setup): Dedicated pool provisioned + basic smoke test passes (SLOs reporting).
Week 1 (ingest & baseline): Data ingestion complete, baseline metrics recorded, initial embedding index created.
Week 2 (experiment): Run reranker on shadow traffic/sample; run 500 manual assistant QA prompts.
Week 3 (evaluation & handoff): Present evaluation report; obtain customer decision: proceed to pilot / iterate / stop.

Instrumented Checks (must ship during POC)
- Per-route traces: token counts, token latency distribution, model variant tag.
- Cost meters: token cost + embedding cost per request.
- Quality checks: automated BLEU/ROUGE is not sufficient — include manual rubric scoring on 100 user flows for assistant.

Technical Plan (high level)
1) Model selection: shortlist two model variants (3B quantized baseline; 7B fallback) with known throughput profiles.
2) Prefix caching: implement session-level KV caching for merchant assistant to reduce repeated prefix recomputation.
3) Embedding store: Pinecone-like approach using dense vectors hosted in customer's VPC (customer comfortable), or use Redwood-managed vector store sandbox (falls back to hosted).
4) Reranker: fast lightweight transformer (distil-based) to rescore top-K candidates returned by initial retrieval.
5) Observability integration: wire up Redwood Console dashboards per route and token-level traces to Datadog (customer uses Datadog).

Operational Guardrails
- Autoscale cap: max GPUs set to 4 for test runs; burst policy disabled.
- Cost alarm: signal when projected monthly spend exceeds the $X cost envelope (configured in console).
- Model fallback: policy to route to 7B model if the 3B variant crosses 95th latency threshold for >5 minutes.

Evaluation Protocols (how we measure)
- Reranking: run paired evaluation with N=10k impressions sampled from the last 48 hours. Compute CTR, NDCG@10, and deltas vs baseline.
- Assistant: create a 100-prompt eval suite representing merchant questions (categorized: payments, inventory, returns). Score on relevance, safety, and actionable correctness (0-3 rubric).

Workshop/TODOs (quick, editable list)
- [ ] Confirm S3 credential expiry window (owner: Customer)
- [ ] Create JIRA board and link tickets (owner: Maya) -> JIRA:SE-1027 created
- [ ] Provision dedicated pool (owner: Platform) - target provision by 2026-02-22
- [ ] Share 100 merchant prompts for baseline (owner: Customer)
- [ ] Setup initial Datadog dashboards (owner: SRE)
- [ ] Draft rollout policy for model fallback (owner: Jordan)

Open Questions (for the kickoff)
- Can the customer accept a hosted vector store for the POC or insist on VPC-only?
- Are there any regulatory red flags for storing 7-day behavioral logs in Redwood-managed infra?
- What's the acceptable sampling rate for shadow traffic to avoid business disruption?

Risk Register (high level)
- Data quality: product catalog mismatch -> mitigation: run catalog consistency checks and synthetic queries.
- Cost runaway: model chosen is too expensive -> mitigation: enforce max GPUs and token caps per-minute.
- Latency spikes: poorly tuned batching -> mitigation: conservative batch size + enable fallback routing.

Deliverables by end of POC
- Technical runbook documenting model variants, prefix caching config, and endpoints used.
- Evaluation report with CTR/NDCG and assistant rubric scores plus sample failures.
- Demo UI with replayable sessions and reranker A/B toggle.
- Handoff checklist for pilot (ops checklist + cost forecast for 30-day projected traffic).

Quick Notes / Scratchpad (informal)
- Customer prefers US-west region; check GPU availability for n1-high with A100-equivalent.
- Slack thread: #harbor-poc has early logs and network test results.
- Consider trying int8 quantization if 8-bit perf not sufficient (but will need rerun QA).

Signoff criteria (customer + Redwood)
- Customer signs off to move to pilot if: (1) both latency AND CTR targets met, and (2) risk mitigations acceptable, and (3) cost forecast within envelope.

Next immediate steps (48 hours)
1) Run provisioning ping with Platform and confirm ETA.
2) Customer to upload sample data + share access.
3) Solutions Eng to prepare initial model perf runbook and schedule the 90m kickoff workshop.

Appendix: shorthand links and artifacts
- Quick perf notes (internal): perf/simulations/harbor-run-2026-02-14.md (internal perf logs)
- Eval prompt set (draft): drive/shared/harbor/eval/assistant-100.csv
- Contact list: Customer PM - Anika Rao; Eng lead - Tomas Li; SRE lead - Priya Kapoor

-- end of doc (working draft)

Notes to self: keep the acceptance matrix strict. If CTR <8% uplift, recommend pausing and going deeper on retrieval quality before scaling.
